item.title: Tolu Young becomes first Fijian to qualify for Commonwealth Games men's 50m freestyle final
item.description: Fiji has reached another historic milestone in international swimming after David Young, also known as Tolu Young, became the first Fijian to qualify for a Commonwealth Games men's 50 metres freestyle final. This is after clocking a blistering personal best time of 22.09 seconds in the semi finals in Glasgow, Scotland.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has reached another historic milestone in international swimming after David Young, also known as Tolu Young, became the first Fijian to qualify for a Commonwealth Games men's 50 metres freestyle final.

This is after clocking a blistering personal best time of 22.09 seconds in the semi finals in Glasgow, Scotland.

Young produced the swim of his career to secure his place in the final, marking a breakthrough moment for Fiji Aquatics and Team Fiji on the international stage.

His performance has been widely celebrated, with Fiji Aquatics describing it as a phenomenal achievement that has made the entire nation proud.

His time of 22.09 seconds is one of Fiji's greatest achievements in international swimming and puts Young in contention for a Commonwealth Games medal.

Young will return to the pool for the men's 50 metres freestyle final, which will be held at 8am tomorrow , as Fiji eagerly awaits another historic performance.

item.title: AIIB approves US$80M in financing to improve Fiji's climate and disaster preparedness
item.description: In a statement the Bank says the funding is being provided under their Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility and is co-financed with the World Bank. They say together, the two institutions will provide US$230 million which is about FJ$516 million in fast-disbursing budget support to help implement the Government's reform programme.
item.content:encoded:
In a statement the Bank says the funding is being provided under their Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility and is co-financed with the World Bank.

They say together, the two institutions will provide US$230 million which is about FJ$516 million in fast-disbursing budget support to help implement the Government's reform programme.

The programme aims to strengthen Fiji's ability to respond to external economic shocks and climate-related disasters while improving the business environment.

It is expected by 2028 to expand disaster risk reduction coverage, improve public financial management for disaster preparedness, increase access to regulated financial services for small and medium-sized businesses, streamline regulations for low-risk tourism operators, expand digital payments, and improve nutrition and physical activity outcomes for children.

AIIB Chief Investment Officer Kim-See Lim says the financing provides timely support for Fiji's reform agenda while strengthening systems needed for long-term economic resilience.

Minister for Finance, Commerce and Business Development Esrom Immanuel welcomed the financing, saying it comes at an important time as Fiji advances key reforms to strengthen the economy and build resilience against future shocks.

He says the support complements the Government's commitment to prudent fiscal management, climate resilience, and creating a more enabling environment for businesses and investment.

The programme aligns with Fiji's National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050 and further strengthens AIIB's partnership with Fiji.

item.title: Naitasiri Rugby Team praised for leading Nausori clean-up as Tabuya urges public to stop littering
item.description: The Naitasiri Rugby Team swapped the rugby field for the streets of Nausori, collecting rubbish as part of a team, bonding exercise and earning praise from Minister for Environment, Lynda Tabuya, who says protecting Fiji's environment is everyone's responsibility. item.content:encoded:
The Naitasiri Rugby Team swapped the rugby field for the streets of Nausori, collecting rubbish as part of a team, bonding exercise and earning praise from Minister for Environment, Lynda Tabuya, who says protecting Fiji's environment is everyone's responsibility.

Tabuya joined the team and handed over clean-up materials, including recyclable sacks, gloves and hand sanitisers, to support the initiative.

She thanked the players for leading by example and wished them every success in their upcoming Skipper Cup matches .

The Minister says people should take responsibility for disposing of their rubbish properly in bins instead of expecting others to clean up after them.

She also encouraged members of the public to speak up when they see someone littering and politely remind them to "Do the Right Thing" by disposing of their rubbish responsibly.

The clean-up campaign highlighted the importance of everyone working together to keep Fiji clean and protect the environment.

item.title: Nadi siblings praised for cleaning up community and supporting Return and Earn initiative
item.description: Jeremiah, Manoa and Elizabeth were on their way home from school when they noticed plastic bottles and empty cans scattered around Solovi. Instead of walking past, they asked a nearby shop for an empty carton, collected the litter, took it home and sorted the recyclables into bags ready to be returned through the Return and Earn programme at the Nadi Town Council next week.
item.content:encoded:
Jeremiah, Manoa and Elizabeth were on their way home from school when they noticed plastic bottles and empty cans scattered around Solovi.

Instead of walking past, they asked a nearby shop for an empty carton, collected the litter, took it home and sorted the recyclables into bags ready to be returned through the Return and Earn programme at the Nadi Town Council next week.

Their efforts immediately made a visible difference to the area and highlighted how simple actions can help keep communities clean.

The Return and Earn programme encourages people to recycle eligible beverage containers, helping to reduce litter while promoting cleaner and more sustainable communities.

The children's actions have been praised as an example of environmental responsibility, showing that no one is too young to make a positive difference.

Members of the public are also being encouraged to collect and return empty bottles and cans through the initiative to help keep Fiji clean for future generations.

item.title: House of Salt crowned 2025 National SME of the Year as Krisneel Deo wins Best Maritime SME Award
item.description: House of Salt was crowned the 2025 National SME of the Year, while Krisneel Deo of Delaivuna Farm Fresh Eggs won the Best Maritime SME of the Year award at the Fiji Development Bank National SME Awards in Suva. Held under the theme "Ignite, Innovate and Inspire," the awards celebrated the resilience, innovation and achievements of Fiji's small and medium enterprises, with 145 businesses submitting
item.content:encoded:
House of Salt was crowned the 2025 National SME of the Year, while Krisneel Deo of Delaivuna Farm Fresh Eggs won the Best Maritime SME of the Year award at the Fiji Development Bank National SME Awards in Suva.

Held under the theme "Ignite, Innovate and Inspire," the awards celebrated the resilience, innovation and achievements of Fiji's small and medium enterprises, with 145 businesses submitting more than 300 entries across eight award categories.

House of Salt also received the Sustainable SME of the Year award, recognising its environmentally and socially responsible business practices, while the prestigious National SME of the Year title acknowledged the company's outstanding business performance, innovation, leadership and growth potential.

Krisneel Deo of Delaivuna Farm Fresh Eggs was recognised as the Best Maritime SME of the Year for demonstrating business excellence, creating meaningful economic opportunities and contributing to the development of Fiji's maritime communities.

Avishay Singh of Sahil's Party Ice and Frozen Supplies won the Best Agri-Business SME of the Year award for excellence, innovation and sustainable growth in agriculture and value-added agricultural products.

Leone Vulaca of Leone Vulaca Prosthetic and Orthotic Centre received the Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year award in recognition of his innovation and strong business growth.

Dr Marilyn Cornelius of Alchemus Prime was named Women Entrepreneur of the Year for her leadership, innovation and business excellence.

Tanisha Lal of NailedIt won the Youth Entrepreneur of the Year award for demonstrating innovation, resilience and excellence in growing her business.

Each category winner received a $5,000 cash prize presented by the respective category sponsors.

The Fiji Development Bank says the awards recognise the important role SMEs play in creating jobs, strengthening communities and driving Fiji's economic growth, while celebrating the entrepreneurs whose vision, determination and innovation continue to build a more resilient and prosperous nation.
